evidence.claim: A Communist Party spokesman said China reserves the right to use force over Taiwan as a last resort, while peaceful reunification remains the first choice.
evidence.title: China says it reserves right to use force over Taiwan
evidence.excerpt: A Communist Party spokesman said China reserves the right to use force over Taiwan as a last resort, while peaceful reunification remains the first choice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire item quoting a party spokesman immediately before the congress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the party-state under Xi, but not a personal nuclear-order statement.
contrary_evidence: The statement includes a peaceful-first formulation.
It is about Taiwan coercion, not nuclear doctrine itself.

evidence.claim: China launched its largest-ever drills around Taiwan, fired missiles near the island, and sharply raised the risk of regional miscalculation after Pelosi's visit.
evidence.title: Furious China fires missiles near Taiwan in drills after Pelosi visit
evidence.excerpt: China launched its largest-ever drills around Taiwan, fired missiles near the island, and sharply raised the risk of regional miscalculation after Pelosi's visit.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire item, even though the republisher page title is noisy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Xi's governing system and Taiwan policy, though the article reports military action rather than a direct Xi quote.
contrary_evidence: The drills were conventional, not nuclear use.
They may be read as signaling rather than immediate escalation to nuclear brinkmanship.

evidence.claim: Xi said the Ukraine crisis was not something China wanted to see and that countries should not come to the point of meeting on the battlefield.
evidence.title: Xi Jinping: Countries should not come to the point of meeting on the battlefield. Conflict and confrontation are not in anyone's interest. Peace and security are what the international community should treasure the most.
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: Xi said the Ukraine crisis was not something China wanted to see and that countries should not come to the point of meeting on the battlefield.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official Xi readout with explicit peace language and date.
contrary_evidence: The call is declaratory and does not show concrete leverage over Russia.
It coexisted with later Chinese non-condemnation of Russia at the UN.

evidence.claim: Xi said China would support Russia and Ukraine resolving the issue through negotiations and reiterated China's consistent position on respecting sovereignty and the UN Charter.
evidence.title: President Xi Jinping Speaks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the Phone
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: Xi said China would support Russia and Ukraine resolving the issue through negotiations and reiterated China's consistent position on respecting sovereignty and the UN Charter.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph / summary of Xi's remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official readout of a dated Xi-Putin phone call.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target-period response to the invasion's start.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi, though the statement is mediated through a bilateral readout.
contrary_evidence: The call did not publicly condemn Russia's invasion.
It echoed Russian security talking points about NATO and legitimacy of Russian concerns.

evidence.claim: China said sovereignty and territorial integrity should be respected, parties should exercise restraint, and diplomatic efforts toward a peaceful settlement should be supported.
evidence.title: Wang Yi Expounds China's Five-Point Position on the Current Ukraine Issue
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: China said sovereignty and territorial integrity should be respected, parties should exercise restraint, and diplomatic efforts toward a peaceful settlement should be supported.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official policy statement, dated immediately after the invasion began.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to Xi as top leader of the Chinese state; this is state policy, not a personal command act.
contrary_evidence: The statement also gave rhetorical space to Russia's 'legitimate security concerns'.
It is not a neutral condemnation of aggression.

evidence.claim: China deployed large-scale military drills and fired live missiles near Taiwan, sharply raising the risk of regional miscalculation after Pelosi's visit.
evidence.title: Furious China fires missiles near Taiwan in drills after Pelosi visit
evidence.excerpt: China deployed large-scale military drills and fired live missiles near Taiwan, sharply raising the risk of regional miscalculation after Pelosi's visit.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire item on a major crisis event with direct operational details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Xi's governing system and Taiwan policy, though not a quoted Xi order.
contrary_evidence: The drills were conventional rather than nuclear.
They can be read as signaling as well as coercion.

evidence.claim: China said it was halting senior-level military dialogue with the United States and suspending other cooperation, including climate talks, in retaliation for Pelosi's Taiwan visit.
evidence.title: China halts high-level military dialogue with U.S., suspends other cooperation
evidence.excerpt: China said it was halting senior-level military dialogue with the United States and suspending other cooperation, including climate talks, in retaliation for Pelosi's Taiwan visit.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting on a specific suspension of channels and mechanisms.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to Xi-era state control over the U.S. relationship and military channels.
contrary_evidence: Suspending dialogue may have been intended as temporary punishment rather than permanent rupture.
This does not prove all backchannel communication ceased.

unresolved_gaps: Direct command-and-control, custody, and launch-discipline evidence is still thin.
Concrete arms-control follow-through beyond declaratory no-first-use language is limited.
Crisis de-escalation evidence in the Taiwan and Russia-Ukraine settings is mostly indirect.
Direct evidence of Xi personally authorizing or restraining specific military moves is thin.
Civilian-protection and operational-conduct evidence during the Taiwan crisis is limited.
Evidence of actual mediation or de-escalation in Russia-Ukraine remains mostly declaratory.
Water, sanitation, and local service-variation evidence is thin compared with health, pensions, housing, and crisis response.
Chain-of-command evidence for specific repression episodes remains limited.
Independent evidence on courts, legislatures, and oversight bodies resisting capture is thin.
Succession and term-limit mechanics could be more directly documented as a de facto transfer-rule breach.
Independent evaluation of implementation quality across provinces and local-government debt stress remains limited.
Distributional evidence beyond averages and poverty-lifted subgroups could be stronger.
Water/sanitation and housing-quality evidence is thinner than health, pensions, and child-welfare evidence.
Independent evaluation of service quality, regional equity, and front-line delivery remains limited.
Direct, ruler-specific evidence on Xi's own assets, gifts, family business interests, or beneficial ownership is missing.
Independent findings on concealment or obstruction tied personally to Xi are absent.
Evidence of truthful correction versus rhetorical anti-corruption messaging is weak.
Independent evaluation of whether loyalist-heavy appointments improved competence or mainly tightened political control is thin.
More subnational evidence on execution quality and correction would strengthen the adaptation story.
Durable causal impact of the COVID rollback and economic stabilization package remains under-audited.
